description: C++17 / C++20 source: function templates, classes with ownership models, STL containers, RAII via destructors, exceptions with noexcept contracts, dynamic_cast / typeid RTTI. Calibrated against fmtlib/fmt (header-only format library) plus hand-authored UB-trap samples. Per ADR-026, one spec per primary template (not per instantiation); the spec's invariants are quantified over the template type parameters. Per ADR-028, the parser sidecar receives a compile_commands.json bootstrapped by CMake when the corpus is CMake-based.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the routine must preserve across all valid inputs. When the routine is a function template, invariants may be quantified over the template type parameters (per ADR-026) — use the `quantifier` field to make the universe explicit, e.g. 'for all T satisfying std::is_arithmetic_v<T>'.

fields.name: quantifier
fields.doc: When the invariant holds only for a subset of T (or for any quantified parameter), describe the subset in plain English. Omit for non-template routines.

fields.name: behavior_on_violation
fields.doc: When the quantifier excludes a T, what happens for that T? compile error | undefined behavior | soft fallback | not_applicable.

fields.name: generatorHints
fields.doc: Optional. Per-claim Hypothesis-style generator hints (per ADR-030). Shape: { inputs:[{name,type,min?,max?,maxLen?,alphabet?}], constraint?:string, examples?:[{...}] }. When present, the 4th validation gate (FALSIFYING) exercises the claim against generated inputs; when absent, the gate skips the claim with skipReason: no_hints.

claimKinds.label: Object lifetime
claimKinds.description: Ownership model for any object the routine creates, accepts, or returns. C++ encodes this through smart-pointer types, references, and lifetime tags. Distinguishes Unique (std::unique_ptr / owning by-value), Shared (std::shared_ptr / shared_ptr-like), Borrowed (reference or non-owning raw pointer), Pinned (must not move — std::pin / address-stable), Automatic (stack-bound). Critical for the .NET / Java translation: Unique maps to IDisposable / AutoCloseable; Shared maps to a reference-count wrapper; Borrowed maps to a method parameter; Pinned typically becomes an Open Question.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: The parameter, member, or local whose lifetime is being claimed.

fields.name: policy
fields.doc: Plain-English description of who owns the object, when it is destroyed, and any aliasing constraints.

claimKinds.label: Template instantiation
claimKinds.description: When the routine is a function template (per ADR-026, the spec describes the primary template, not each instantiation). This claim records the SFINAE / Concepts constraint(s) that gate which Ts are legal, plus a curated list of Ts the corpus actually instantiates. The Migration Planner reads `instantiations_observed` to prioritise which Ts the test pack must exercise; it is informational, not signed.

fields.name: template_parameters
fields.doc: Verbatim parameter list, e.g. 'typename T' or 'typename T, std::size_t N'.

fields.name: constraint
fields.doc: SFINAE / Concepts requirement on the parameters; 'none' when the template accepts any T. e.g. 'requires std::is_arithmetic_v<T>'.

fields.name: instantiations_observed
fields.doc: Curated list of Ts the corpus instantiates this template with (informational; not signed).

claimKinds.label: Undefined behavior
claimKinds.description: Inputs or states that cause the C++ standard's undefined behavior. Surfacing these explicitly is critical for migration: a routine that *relies on* UB (e.g., wraparound on signed overflow) breaks when translated naively. Each UB claim should record the trigger, the standard reference (when known), and whether the routine handles or assumes-no-UB.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: Plain-English description of the input or state that causes UB.

fields.name: routine_assumption
fields.doc: Does the routine assume the caller never triggers this, defensively guard against it, or actively exploit the UB (e.g. wraparound)?

claimKinds.label: Exception contract
claimKinds.description: The routine's exception-safety guarantee and which exception types it can throw. Maps to .NET (C# exceptions) and Java (checked / unchecked) — `noexcept` typically maps to non-throwing signatures, basic / strong guarantees inform the scaffold's try-catch structure.

fields.name: guarantee
fields.doc: NoThrow = noexcept or proven non-throwing; Basic = invariants preserved on throw, leaks possible; Strong = transactional rollback on throw; NoneStated = the routine does not document its guarantee.

fields.name: exception_types
fields.doc: Exception types the routine can throw (e.g. ['std::format_error', 'std::bad_alloc']).

fields.name: contract
fields.doc: Plain-English description of when each exception is thrown and what state it leaves behind.

claimKinds.label: RTTI usage
claimKinds.description: Run-time type dispatch the routine relies on: `dynamic_cast`, `typeid`, virtual-dispatch through a base reference, std::any / std::variant visitor unwrap. These have target-language analogues (C# `is` / `as`, Java `instanceof`) but the semantics often differ — particularly for std::variant which has no clean Java equivalent.

fields.name: reflection_pattern
fields.doc: Plain-English description of how the RTTI is used and what runtime decision it makes.

fields.name: translation_hint
fields.doc: Suggested mapping (e.g. 'C# 12 pattern matching with sealed hierarchy' or 'Java 17 sealed interface + switch').

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: I/O writes, allocations from caller-supplied allocators, std::cout / iostream output, file-system operations, thread-local / global mutations.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary and failure-mode conditions the routine handles (or is silent about). C++-specific edges include: empty std::vector / std::string_view, std::vector<bool>'s proxy reference, NaN propagation in floating-point, integer-promotion surprises (bool + bool = int), iterator invalidation across container mutations, and the std::move semantics around the moved-from object.

fields.name: generatorHints
fields.doc: Optional. Per-claim Hypothesis-style generator hints (per ADR-030). Same shape as on invariant. When present, the 4th gate exercises this edge case against generated inputs that satisfy the hint constraint; when absent, the gate skips the claim with skipReason: no_hints.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities the source does not resolve and the SME must answer before sign-off. Common C++ cases: ownership intent of raw pointer parameters, whether a moved-from object is re-used, template parameter constraints that don't map to Java generics (force a JNA fallback per ADR-027), and platform-specific UB the corpus relies on.

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_class
topLevelFields.doc: When the routine is a class method, the fully-qualified class name (e.g. 'fmt::detail::format_context').

topLevelFields.name: namespace
topLevelFields.doc: The enclosing namespace path (e.g. 'fmt::detail'). Empty for the global namespace.

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: C++ parameter mode. `in` = pass-by-value or const-ref (read-only); `in_out` = non-const reference (read+write); `out` = non-const reference whose initial value is ignored; `return` = the function's return value.

promptHints.emphasis: When the routine is a function template, emit exactly ONE templateInstantiation claim describing the primary template's parameters and constraint (per ADR-026). Quantify invariants over the type parameters; if an invariant holds only for a subset of T, name the subset in the `quantifier` field. Always emit an exceptionContract claim — `noexcept` and 'no guarantee stated' are both signal. When the routine relies on undefined behavior (signed wraparound, type-punning via union, use-after-move with intent), file an undefinedBehavior claim with category set. For ownership: prefer `Unique` for std::unique_ptr / owning by-value, `Shared` for std::shared_ptr, `Borrowed` for references / non-owning raw pointers. When ownership of a raw pointer parameter is ambiguous, file an openQuestion — do NOT guess.
